answer: Latency-seeded identity cost. Each new identity must complete a random walk of interactions whose depth grows with the count of identities sharing its creation epoch; verification latency compounds along that vine of hops. Attacker cost is per-identity waiting time plus fees paid at every hop, and identities that wander across epochs pay full path cost again. A lotus flag marks epochs exceeding a cap, freezing new identity issuance until the epoch's oldest identities age out.
